**A blues scale in the key of A (A blues)**  

| Scale degree | Note | Interval from previous note |
|--------------|------|-----------------------------|
| 1 (root)     | **A** | – |
| ♭3 (blue note) | **C** | minor 3rd (3 semitones) |
| 4 (perfect 4th) | **D** | whole step (2 semitones) |
| ♭5 (flat‑5th) | **D♯** | half step (1 semitone) |
| 5 (perfect 5th) | **E** | half step (1 semitone) |
| ♭7 (blue note) | **G** | minor 3rd (3 semitones) |
| (back to 1)  | **A** | whole step (2 semitones) |

**Pattern in interval form**

```
1   –   ♭3   –   4   –   ♭5   –   5   –   ♭7   –   1
m3  –   W    –   H    –   H    –   m3   –   W
```

So the A blues scale is:

**A – C – D – D♯ – E – G – A**

It’s essentially the A minor pentatonic (A, C, D, E, G) with an added “blue” note, the flat‑5th (D♯). This pattern works the same in any key; just shift the notes up or down to match the desired root.
